correctness.rationale: The proof rewrites the objective as maximizing \(s=h+v\). Feasibility is equivalent to \(q\ge3p-4\). In the first regime, \(h+3v\le q-3p+4\) directly bounds \(s\), with equality at \((q-3p+4,0)\). In the second regime, \(2s\le q-2p+4\) is sharp except when \(q\equiv2\pmod4\); equality there would force \(h-v=p\) but gives opposite parities for \(s\) and \(p\), so one unit is lost. Explicit residue-class witnesses attain every stated bound. An independent finite enumerator agrees for all \(2\le p\le30\), \(p<q\le150\), and reproduces the source tables/corollaries. Risk: finite replay cannot certify the infinite theorem, so acceptance rests on the algebraic proof, whose boundary cases and integrality conditions were separately checked.

value.rationale: The source treats the optimization as an integer-programming step and publishes only low-parameter consequences. Closing that optimization for all torus-knot parameters removes the solver dependency, gives a precise feasibility threshold, exposes a non-obvious mod-four obstruction, and supplies explicit optimal witnesses. These are structural facts about a natural published construction, not an arbitrary finite slice. The value is bounded: the theorem improves understanding and reproducibility of the one-braid bound but does not make that bound globally optimal among all toric-mosaic constructions.
